analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction about two overdraft fees totalling £30 allegedly caused by a late salary credit, which is a financial loss (CH-1).
analysis.summary: The customer's salary did not arrive on 30 September. Her account went overdrawn and two unarranged overdraft fees of £15 were charged (30/09 and 01/10). She asks for the £30 to be refunded. The handler's check of the incident log found INC-4471, a batch delay on inbound Faster Payments on 30/09, with credits applied on 01/10. The fees are confirmed. No vulnerability indicators were found. The complaint has been acknowledged and is on track.

timeline.event: Expected salary did not arrive; incident INC-4471 batch delay on inbound Faster Payments occurred; first £15 unarranged overdraft fee charged
Delayed credits applied; second £15 unarranged overdraft fee charged
Complaint received by email and logged; incident log checked and fees confirmed

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss is £30, under £100, with no other CH-6 high or medium triggers (no fraud, vulnerability, repeat contact or legal threat). A possible wider issue exists via the batch delay incident, but there is no evidence of many customers complaining.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None needed at present; customer said she is fine. Continue to watch for indicators.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger: not fraud, lending, vulnerability referral, legal or media threat, or app failure needing technical investigation. The incident is already identified and documented, so the handler can resolve it. The handler may consider whether Senior Complaints Review should be told of the incident's wider impact.

policy_citations.quote: Where a fee was charged because of a bank error (for example a system fault, an incorrect tariff or a payment the bank failed to process on time), the fee must be refunded in full
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The fees appear linked to bank incident INC-4471, so the handler should assess whether this is a bank error under FEE-2. The decision rests with the handler.

policy_citations.quote: *Low*: financial loss under £100 or a service issue with no loss.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The loss is £30, so severity is Low.
The complaint centres on overdraft fees, so the primary root cause is Fees and charges.

policy_citations.quote: Decisions on whether a complaint is upheld, and on any redress, must be made by an authorised complaints handler or specialist.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: This analysis does not state an outcome; the handler decides.

evidence.quote: you charged me two unarranged overdraft fees of £15 each
INC-4471 batch delay on inbound Faster Payments 30/09, credits applied 01/10
No vulnerability indicators, cust says she's fine just annoyed.

handover.complaint_summary: Customer's salary was delayed on 30/09 because of a bank batch delay (INC-4471). Two £15 unarranged overdraft fees were charged. She requests a £30 refund.
handover.desired_outcome: Refund of the £30 in overdraft fees
actions_taken: Two £15 unarranged overdraft fees confirmed on 30/09 and 01/10
Acknowledgement letter sent by email on 2026-10-28
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No indicators found; customer said she is fine, so she appears to have been asked.
open_questions: Is the delay on the customer's salary confirmed as caused by INC-4471 rather than the employer?
Were any other charges or interest applied because of the overdraft?
Does the incident affect other customers?

other_gaps: Received 2026-10-27 with 43 days left, On track
